walks.name: Mission
walks.vibe: Murals, palm trees and the friendliest windows in town. This is where it all began.

start.n: Where the first walk began. 16th St BART is a block east if you come by train.

stops.n: Coffee shop with a busy board just south of 16th. Pin one at eye level and grab a cup for the road.
Go door to door from 16th to 20th. Bookshops, vintage and little cafes say yes the most. Leave one wherever someone smiles.
A curiosity shop near 19th. Ask it and the shops beside it about window space.
Pause for a scoop, then carry it up the block to the park.
Find a spot on the hill by the palms, look back at the skyline, and count how many flyers you left behind.

bonus.n: Hit the big boards at Rainbow, or keep going down Valencia. 24th Street has its own walk.

walks.name: 24th Street
walks.vibe: Calle 24: panaderias, murals, papel picado and shopkeepers who know everyone.

start.n: Right at 24th St BART. Walk east toward the murals.

stops.n: A coffee and a board in one stop, steps from BART.
Go door to door toward Bryant. Small family shops here often say yes, and some are glad to have a flyer in Spanish too.
A neighborhood market with a board.
A block south. Sit by the trees and catch your breath.

walks.name: Haight-Ashbury
walks.vibe: Bookstores, vintage and a famous hill in the park to end the day.

start.n: Start at the east end and walk toward the park.

stops.n: A big cafe board, just off Haight.
Collective bookstore, a natural home for notices.
Ask the vintage and record stores. They love flyers.
A must-hit board near the park end. Amoeba is a few blocks on at 1855 Haight.
A short detour to Cole Valley for a proper soda fountain scoop.
Into Golden Gate Park. Drums, sun, grass.

walks.name: Castro
walks.vibe: Rainbow crosswalks, a big neighborhood board and lots of foot traffic.

start.n: Castro Muni station, under the big flag.

stops.n: Shops around the corner are used to event posters. Ask for a window spot.
Coffee and a board in one stop.
Swing over to Sanchez for one more board.
A short climb to a rocky top with the whole city below you.

walks.name: Hayes Valley
walks.vibe: Boutiques, a little green in the middle of it all, and ice cream around the corner.

start.n: Right at Patricia's Green.

stops.n: Corner cafe with a board, a short walk south on Octavia.
Small-batch ice cream, a block from the green.
Design shops like a nice-looking poster. Ask for the window.
A few blocks west on Hayes.
Back to the green. Watch the skaters, rest your feet.

walks.name: Noe Valley
walks.vibe: Strollers, bakeries and a town square that's practically made for notices.

start.n: The J Church stops right here. Walk west up 24th.

stops.n: From Church to Diamond it's all small shops. Owners know their regulars, so ask warmly.
Something warm for the walk.
Benches, sun, and a community board right there. Post one, then sit.

bonus.n: Two laundromats a few blocks south.

walks.name: Lower Haight
walks.vibe: Bars, records and cafes, with two parks that both have boards.

start.n: The 22 Fillmore and the 7 Haight both stop here.

stops.n: Classic spot with a packed board.
A few doors down.
Record shops and bars love gig and event flyers.
Another cafe board on the way.
A little park board on Page St.
A board by the playground, and grass for the dogs and you.

walks.name: Mission Dolores
walks.vibe: Quiet blocks, old church bells and laundromats with very readable walls.

start.n: Right by the J Church stop.

stops.n: A bakery board on Church. Grab a pastry while you're in there.
Over to Guerrero. The laundromat crowd has time to read.
Corner shops and cafes between 16th and 20th. Ask nicely, leave one in the window.
Neighborhood coffee spot with a board.
One more laundromat on Dolores St on your way to the park.

stops.t: Dolores Park, top of the hill
stops.n: Sit up near Church and 20th for one of the best views in the city.

walks.name: Inner Sunset
walks.vibe: Foggy mornings, the N Judah rumbling by, and Golden Gate Park a block away.

start.n: The N Judah stops right here.

stops.n: Grocery board a few doors up.
Small-batch scoops right on 9th.
Walk Irving from 5th to 11th. Lots of small owners.
Grocery board on Irving.
Head north on 9th into the park. Find a tree.

walks.name: NOPA and Panhandle
walks.vibe: The Painted Ladies, Divisadero's cafes and a long green strip to wander.

start.n: Start at the park, facing the famous row of Victorians.

stops.n: On the Hayes St side of the park.
Cafes and shops between Hayes and Oak. Ask for windows.
Grocery board by the door.
Two laundromats about six blocks apart. Hit both.
Old neighborhood cafe. Warm drink, one more board.
Walk the long green strip toward Golden Gate Park.

walks.name: Bernal Heights
walks.vibe: One sweet main street, a hill with a radio tower, and classic ice cream at the bottom.

start.n: The heart of Cortland. Everything here is a short walk.

stops.n: Coffee and laundry, across the street from each other.
The neighborhood grocer and its well loved board.
A small-town strip where every shopkeeper knows everyone, so word travels.
At the east end of Cortland.
Climb up for the view all the way around. Golden hour is lovely here.
Head down the west side for a scoop at the city's classic, open since 1953.

walks.name: North Beach
walks.vibe: Poets, espresso and a tower on the hill.

start.n: Under the neon, by the bookstore.

stops.n: The Beat generation's bookstore. Ask about their board.
Espresso where the poets wrote.
Tiny old shops. Ask, and you might hear a story.
A neighborhood grocery board on Green St.
Lie on the grass under the church spires. There's a board here too.

walks.name: Glen Park and CCSF
walks.vibe: A tiny village by a canyon, with a whole college campus nearby.

start.n: Step out of the station and you're in the village.

stops.n: Neighborhood bookstore with a board.
The local grocery. Ask at the front.
Coffee at Diamond and Chenery, open Tuesday to Sunday mornings. Another place to ask.
Wander into the canyon. Rocks, creek, eucalyptus. Breathe.

bonus.n: Flyers on campus need approval first. Drop by Student Activities.

walks.name: Ocean Ave and City College
walks.vibe: Students, the K streetcar, and a busy little main street by City College.

start.t: Ocean Ave and Frida Kahlo Way
start.n: Right by City College's Ocean campus.
start.a: Ocean Ave and Frida Kahlo Way

stops.n: Coffee shop board near campus.
A small plaza on Ocean. A good spot to sit for a minute.
A laundromat board a few blocks west.
Cafes, bakeries and small shops toward 19th Ave. Students pass here all day.
A neighborhood bakery for the walk back.

bonus.n: Keep going west to Lakeside Village.

walks.name: Inner Richmond
walks.vibe: Clement Street: dumplings, bookstores and a crepe stop.

start.n: The 2 Clement runs right along here.

stops.n: Begin with something sweet.
A much loved bookstore with a busy board.
Right next door.
Bakeries, markets and gift shops to ask, all the way to 12th.
A quiet lake a few blocks north.

walks.name: Duboce Triangle
walks.vibe: Upper Market, the N Judah portal, and a park full of neighbors and dogs.

start.n: Church St Muni station. Walk north on Church.

stops.n: Shops and cafes between Church and Sanchez. Ask for a window spot.
Small businesses between Market and Duboce. Keep it friendly and quick.
A cafe at the corner of the park.
The park's community board. Neighbors check it on their dog walks.
Sit on the grass and watch the N Judah roll by.

walks.name: Pacific Heights and Polk
walks.vibe: Grand houses, a hilltop park, and Polk Street's bookstores.

start.n: Start on Upper Fillmore.

stops.n: A cozy bookstore board.
A block up. Stairs, views, a breather before Polk.
Over on Polk.
Another board up the block.
Lots of independents between Broadway and Union.
Finish with a scoop at the original, up on Hyde.

walks.name: Outer Sunset
walks.vibe: Surf shops, cozy cafes, salt air and the edge of the city.

start.n: Ride the N Judah to the end of the line.

stops.n: Worker-owned grocery with a great board.
Next door. A wall of local notices.

stops.t: Surf and coffee shops on Judah
stops.n: People out here are relaxed and friendly. Ask away.
Walk to the sand. Sit, breathe, done.

walks.name: Potrero Hill
walks.vibe: A sunny hilltop village with views of downtown.

start.n: Bottom of the hill. It's a climb, but a pretty one.

stops.n: Begin with coffee and a board.
Neighborhood pizza place with a community feel.
Small shops up top. Neighbors read everything.
The hill's grocery board.
Right on 20th.
Sit with the skyline in front of you.

walks.name: Marina and Cow Hollow
walks.vibe: Union and Chestnut, sailboats, and the Golden Gate in view.

start.n: Start up in Cow Hollow and walk down to the water.

stops.n: Grocery board on Union.
Ask the shops on your way down Fillmore.
Down on Chestnut. Coffee and a board.
A block further.
Walk to the water and look at the bridge.

walks.name: West Portal
walks.vibe: A small-town main street at the end of the tunnel, with three boards within a block.

start.n: The K, L and M come out of the tunnel right here.
start.a: West Portal Ave and Ulloa St

stops.n: A comic shop with a board. A 2025 fire sent it to 79 W Portal for a while, so look at both.
Right next door. Donut holes and coffee.
Across the street, another board.

stops.t: Window walk down West Portal Ave
stops.n: Bookshops, cafes and family businesses for three blocks. Ask wherever it feels friendly.
One more board near the far end.
A little green just off the main street.

walks.name: Dogpatch and Mission Bay
walks.vibe: Old warehouses, cranes on the bay and a park by the water.

start.n: By the Caltrain station.

stops.n: Mission Bay board.
Another Mission Bay board.
Small shops and makers. Ask for windows.
The neighborhood hardware store board.
End by the water, next to the giant old cranes.

walks.name: Outer Richmond
walks.vibe: Cozy cafes, a beloved ice cream shop and ruins by the sea.

start.n: The 38 Geary gets you here.

stops.n: A family-run favorite. Begin with a scoop.
Cozy cafe with a board.
Further out on Geary.
Simple Pleasures and La Promenade, a few blocks apart.
End at the old ruins at the edge of the city. Sunsets here are unreal.

walks.name: Excelsior
walks.vibe: A lively Mission Street with panaderías, families and laundromats every few blocks.

start.n: The 14 Mission bus runs the whole route.

stops.n: Family shops, bakeries and phone stores. A Spanish version of your flyer goes a long way here.
Two laundromats almost side by side. Hit both.
Any bakery on Mission St with a warm case. Pan dulce for the walk.
One of the city's biggest, wildest parks, just east. Find a bench with a view.

walks.name: Parkside and Taraval
walks.vibe: The L Taraval line, quiet avenues, and laundromat boards every few blocks.

start.n: The L Taraval runs the whole way, so hop on and off as you like.

stops.n: First laundromat board of the walk.
A mailbox shop with a board.
Keep heading west.
Another laundromat crowd with time to read.
Head south to the lake. There's a community board at the Sloat and Vale entrance, then a quiet path by the water.

bonus.n: Keep going west on Taraval toward the beach.

walks.name: Embarcadero and Salesforce Park
walks.vibe: The Ferry Building, office crowds, and a park four stories up.

start.n: Start at the clock tower on the Embarcadero.

stops.n: An ice cream counter inside the Ferry Building.
Across the plaza, a board for the office crowd.
Another board a couple of blocks in.
Up in Salesforce Park.
Walk the garden loop above the street. Quiet, green and calm.

walks.name: Japantown
walks.vibe: Peace Plaza, the Japan Center malls and a pagoda over it all.

start.n: Post St and Buchanan St, under the pagoda.

stops.n: The pedestrian block north of Post. Small shops, ask at the counter.
Shops along the indoor walkways. Some owners are happy to tape one up.
Matcha soft serve in the Kinokuniya building.
Cross Geary and try the cafes on Fillmore.
Sit by the pagoda for a quiet minute.

walks.name: Tenderloin and Little Saigon
walks.vibe: Dense blocks and busy laundromats around Little Saigon.

start.n: Little Saigon runs along Larkin here.

stops.n: A laundromat board on Eddy.
Last board, up on Jones. Map listings mix it with a cafe, so check it is still a laundromat.
A neighborhood park with benches and a garden.

walks.name: Bayview
walks.vibe: Third Street, the T line, and the wildest shoreline in the city.

start.n: The T Third stops nearby.

stops.n: A laundromat board on Third.
Small businesses along Third. Ask nicely and keep it short.
A community center with a board.
A cafe near the water for a bite.
Sit by the bay and watch the shorebirds.

walks.name: Portola
walks.vibe: San Bruno Ave, the old greenhouse district, and laundromat boards all along it.

start.t: San Bruno Ave and Silver Ave
start.n: The 8 and 9 buses run down San Bruno.
start.a: San Bruno Ave and Silver Ave

stops.n: First board on the avenue.
A cafe at the corner of Burrows.
A couple of blocks south.
Bakeries and small shops. Ask for a window spot.
stops.a: San Bruno Ave and Felton St

stops.n: Head west into the city's second-biggest park.
